manifest_text:
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=68"]
build-backend = "setuptools.backends.legacy:build"

[project]
name = "aspose-html-foss"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Open-source Python toolkit for HTML parsing, DOM manipulation, and serialization."
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
license = {text = "MIT"}
authors = [
    {name = "Aspose.HTML FOSS contributors"},
]
keywords = ["html", "dom", "parser", "css", "aspose"]
classifiers = [
    "Development Status :: 3 - Alpha",
    "Intended Audience :: Developers",
    "License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.10",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
    "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.13",
    "Topic :: Text Processing :: Markup :: HTML",
]
dependencies = [
    "skia-python>=87.0,<145",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
js = ["quickjs>=1.19,<2"]
test = ["pytest>=8"]

[project.urls]
Homepage = "https://github.com/aspose-html-foss/Aspose.HTML-FOSS-for-Python"
Repository = "https://github.com/aspose-html-foss/Aspose.HTML-FOSS-for-Python"
Issues = "https://github.com/aspose-html-foss/Aspose.HTML-FOSS-for-Python/issues"

[tool.setuptools.packages.find]
where = ["src"]

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
pythonpath = ["src"]
testpaths = ["tests"]

contributing.content:
# Contributing

Thank you for your interest in contributing to Aspose.HTML FOSS for Python.

## Development Setup

```bash
python -m venv .venv
. .venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install -e .[test]
```

## Running Tests

```bash
python -m pytest
```

## Guidelines

- Keep public APIs documented with runnable examples when practical.
- Add or update tests for behavioral changes.
- Prefer small, focused changes.
- Follow the existing package layout and naming conventions.
- Do not include generated caches, local environment files, credentials, or private tooling output.

## Reporting Issues

Please use GitHub issues with a minimal reproduction, expected behavior, actual behavior, and Python version.
